Arabidopsis Atlas · Metabolome × Spaceflight

What the terrestrial metabolome says about plants in orbit

Three published natural-variation metabolome GWAS panels — seeds, leaves under control and stress, and leaves before and after six days of darkness — are combined and then linked to the OSD-522 spaceflight transcriptome and proteome of Col-0 shoots grown on the ISS.

Richard Barker · Arabidopsis thaliana · $n_wu Wu, $n_zhu Zhu accessions · OSD-522: $n_rna_tested genes, $n_prot protein records in two fractions

Open the 3D atlas Code & data (GitHub) OSD-522 on NASA OSDR

Overview

OSD-522 measured transcripts and proteins, not metabolites. This links what is known on the ground to what was measured in flight.

NASA's Open Science Data Repository holds no plant metabolomics. What it does hold is the transcriptome and proteome of plants grown in space. Natural-variation metabolome studies tell us which genes control which metabolites, how much accessions differ, and how leaf metabolism responds to darkness and stress. Joining the two asks: when a plant goes to space, do the genes behind each metabolite class move, and where does the flown genotype sit in the terrestrial range?

PyDESeq2 on GeneLab's counts finds $n_rna_sig genes changed at FDR < 0.05 ($n_rna_up up, $n_rna_down down). Wu et al. list reference biosynthesis genes for five metabolite classes; each set is tested by relabelling the 12 samples in all 924 possible ways, which respects co-regulation between pathway genes.

Caveats

Lower biosynthesis-gene expression does not tell you which way a metabolite pool moved; free amino acids, for instance, can rise from protein breakdown while synthesis genes fall. BRIC-LED is lit, so flight is not darkness. Flight plants were 10-day seedlings; Zhu's were 35-day soil-grown plants; Wu's growth stage has not been checked. Naake's loci are wide (together covering ~$naake_cov% of protein-coding genes), so no genome-wide gene-overlap test is attempted. Wu's "amines" gene list includes general genes such as RNA-polymerase subunits.
